Definition: from a compound of G575 and a compound of κάρα (the head) and G1380 (in the sense of watching); intense anticipation:--earnest expectation.
BiblicalUsage: Twice, and both times about waiting with the head stretched forward. Paul's earnest expectation in Philippians 1:20 is that Christ shall be magnified in his body, whether by life or by death, and the earnest expectation of the creature in Romans 8:19 waits for the manifestation of the sons of God.
TheologicalSignificance: The word is a neck craned toward the horizon; creation itself is watching for what God will do next.
